\title{16 Component Dirac Fermion Condensate Singlet Superfluid on \SIG{4+4}{7+1} Spacetime}

\author{Patrick Lee Nash, Ph.D.}
\affiliation{Independent researcher}

\date{November 12, 2026}

\begin{abstract}
%%<1644>
Can a 16-component Dirac field on a flat spacetime with four space-like and four time-like dimensions
form a spin-singlet superfluid, and can that superfluid be the Higgs field, the dark matter, or the
remedy of the Hubble tension? We prove the properties of the eight real $16\times16$ Dirac matrices of
this spacetime, including that their scaled commutators generate $\Pin(4,4)$, and show that the field
evolves unitarily only when it does not depend on the three additional times. In that sector we invent
a complex scalar field, the Vorton-Scalar, which gives the fermions their mass and whose neutral
current couples to their axial current with a constant of Fermi type. Its exchange pairs the fermions.
With the effective action of Cornwall, Jackiw and Tomboulis we obtain the gap, the critical temperature
and the order parameter, a four-vector of a hidden $SO(4)$ symmetry whose component along the hidden
space-like coordinate is the singlet. Simulations with a purpose-built Einstein-Boltzmann solver show
that the model explains neither the Hubble tension nor the galactic phenomenology of dark matter. The
Higgs hypothesis has no geometric basis in this spacetime.
%%</1644>
%%<1671>
Can a 16-component Dirac field on a flat spacetime with seven space-like dimensions and one time-like
dimension form a spin-singlet superfluid, and can that superfluid be the Higgs field, the dark matter,
or the remedy of the Hubble tension? We prove the properties of the eight real $16\times16$ Dirac
matrices of this spacetime, including that their scaled commutators generate $\Pin(7,1)$ and that no
real chirality exists. We invent a complex scalar field, the Vorton-Scalar, which gives the fermions
their mass and whose neutral current couples to their axial current with a constant of Fermi type. Its
exchange pairs the fermions. With the effective action of Cornwall, Jackiw and Tomboulis we obtain the
gap, the critical temperature and the order parameter, a four-vector of the rotations of the four
extra space dimensions. Its condensate breaks $SO(4)$ to $SO(3)$, the pattern of the Higgs vacuum, but
none of the dynamical conditions for a Higgs field is met where the model can be solved. Simulations
with a purpose-built Einstein-Boltzmann solver show that the model explains neither the Hubble tension
nor the galactic phenomenology of dark matter.
%%</1671>
\end{abstract}
